newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil premiums firm on good demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil premiums firm on good demand.

text.p: Good northern European demand for heating oil and scarcity of prompt non-Russian material raised NWE gas oil premiums by over $1 a tonne in steady volume on Friday, traders said.
"The market came up quite nicely," said one cargo trader.
Benchmark Feb IPE futures closed down $4.50 at $226.25 a tonne as temperatures in Europe climbed back to normal levels after a cold snap. The Jan contract expired at $231.75 a tonne
Finished Russian heating oil was offered at least $1 firmer at Feb +$9/10 for prompt and Feb Ipe +$6/7 for late January, with ordinary Russian around $1 lower.
German winter grade 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil was $1 firmer at Feb IPE +$9.50/11 for prompt, with a parcel traded at Feb IPE +$10.25 cif Kiel, but offers were hard to find.
A low sulphur diesel cargo traded at Feb $14 cif Le Havre while another with wax additive went at Feb IPE +$16 cif Hamburg, exhausting most of the NWE demand.

Barges were active, with heating oil done at Feb IPE +$6, Jan IPE +$4 and +$4.50. Ice problems on ARA are due to ease with higher temperatures but some traders heard speculation about the possibility of force majeure on the IPE delivery.
